shrinking each radius preserves absolute convergence. Finite dimensional

has a real open overlap (take real parts). On a real product box the two
extensions agree. Repeated one-variable analytic uniqueness gives equality
on a complex product neighborhood; analytic continuation on the connected
convex overlap gives equality throughout it. Periodic translates agree by
the same argument. A finite cover and strict shrink produce r,a,M>0 with
  |F(z,w)|<=M on a neighborhood of
  {|z-tau|<=r} x {Re(w) in Q, ||Im(w)||_infinity<=a}.
The bounded closed tube lies strictly inside the domain of the extension.

Let fhat(z,k)=integral_Q F(z,x) exp(-2*pi*i*k.x)dx.
Dominated parameter differentiation gives holomorphy in z. Successive
rectangle contour shifts x_j -> x_j-i*a*sign(k_j) cancel periodic vertical
edges and give |fhat(z,k)|<=M exp(-2*pi*a*|k|_1). Cauchy estimates on a
strictly smaller time disc give some R>0 and M1<infinity such that
  |partial_t^m fhat(tau,k)|/m! <= M1 R^(-m) exp(-2*pi*a*|k|_1).
Every fixed mixed derivative of the inverse series is normally summable
on smaller tubes, since polynomial lattice weights times exponential decay
are summable. Explicitly, for c>0 and each d>=0, the one-dimensional series
sum_(n>=0) n^d exp(-cn) converges; finite binomial expansion handles (1+n)^d.
Split an integer sum into its nonnegative and negative restrictions. Then
  1+|k|_1 <= product_j(1+|k_j|),
  exp(-c|k|_1)=product_j exp(-c|k_j|),
and nonnegative product-sum factorization proves the Z^3 majorant summable.
Parameter integral and locally uniform sum differentiation
therefore represent actual derivatives, not formal coefficient operations.

Joint analyticity is certified explicitly. The native bound |m(k)|<=1 follows
from |k|_2^2>=1 for k!=0, with m(0)=0. Set a_mk=partial_t^m fhat(tau,k)/m!.
The coefficient of s^m h^alpha in the inverse series is
  c_(m,alpha)=sum_k m(k) a_mk exp(2*pi*i*k.x0)
                     product_j (2*pi*i*k_j)^alpha_j/alpha_j!.
For |s|<R and ||h||_infinity<a,
  sum_(k,m,alpha) |m(k)a_mk s^m|
       product_j (2*pi*|k_j|*|h_j|)^alpha_j/alpha_j!
  <= M1/(1-|s|/R) * sum_k exp(-2*pi*(a-||h||_infinity)*|k|_1) < infinity.

give a genuine four-variable power series. Absolute rearrangement identifies
